findings.title: Reschedule cleanup uses async forEach and is not awaited
findings.body: Making getCalendar async was handled by marking the forEach callback async and awaiting inside it. Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch only covers the synchronous call, so getCalendar rejections and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. The handler then sends the reschedule email and returns true while calendar deletes and video-meeting deletes are still in flight (or not started). On a serverless runtime that freezes after the response, those external events are often left behind after the booking is already marked CANCELLED.

findings.title: WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video deletes
findings.body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach was changed to async so it can await getCalendar, but forEach does not await that promise and the try/catch around it cannot see later rejections. calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting are therefore fire-and-forget. The function continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns true without those calls finishing, so a cancelled booking can keep its old calendar event and video meeting, and import or API errors are unhandled.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for integration teardown
findings.body: requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach ignores the promises, nothing collects them, and there is no try/catch. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks and resolves successfully while calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting may still be running or may never run if the process is frozen after the response. Organizers can be left with a cancelled booking whose external calendar event and video meeting were not removed, and a failed dynamic import surfaces as an unhandled rejection rather than a failed mutation.

findings.title: Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions
findings.body: The all-remaining-bookings branch still uses forEach(async) and now awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent. That callback is not collected or awaited, and it pushes the resolved deleteEvent result onto apiDeletes only after the await. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) evaluates concat synchronously, before those callbacks resume, so the snapshot does not include the recurring deletes. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of, await getCalendar, and push the delete promise. Recurring cancellations can therefore return after marking bookings CANCELLED without deleting each occurrence from the connected calendars, and getCalendar failures are unhandled rejections.

findings.title: Video adapter import sits outside the Cal Video fallback
findings.body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters before the try block that falls back to createMeetingWithCalVideo and sends the broken-integration email. getVideoAdapters now awaits a dynamic import(), so a rejected app module throws out of createMeeting entirely. Previously that lookup could not fail at request time. A single broken or missing video integration then fails booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video. The same uncovered await is at updateMeeting (line 111) and deleteMeeting (line 144): an import rejection fails reschedule or cancel cleanup instead of being handled per credential.

findings.title: One app import failure fails every calendar lookup
findings.body: getCalendar awaits appStore[type] with no try/catch. A rejected dynamic import now rejects the returned promise, whereas the old synchronous registry lookup only returned null for an unimplemented service. getCachedResults does await Promise.all on every calendar credential's getCalendar call, so one bad integration rejects the whole availability fetch and the booking page cannot compute busy times from the other calendars. createEvent and updateEvent likewise await getCalendar outside their create/update catch blocks, so an import failure aborts EventManager instead of recording a failed result for that credential only.
